brief.subject: Diesel drops 19 cents as cargo theft cases pile up
brief.headline: Diesel falls to $5.937, two big cargo theft cases hit court, LA-Long Beach deal
brief.dek: Fuel relief continues, theft prosecutions mount, a port strike is averted, and a key broker liability case moves forward.
brief.lede: Diesel fell 19.0 cents to $5.937 a gallon, extending a four-week slide. Meanwhile, two federal theft cases show how crooks exploit legitimate freight.

sections.heading: Diesel slide keeps going
bullets: $5.937 per gallon: the U.S. average retail diesel price for the week of 2026-11-16.
Down 19.0 cents (3.1%) week over week, a meaningful cut to per-mile fuel costs.
Down 33.9 cents over four weeks, so revisit fuel surcharge math on spot quotes.

sections.heading: Cargo theft cases stack up
bullets: $7.2 million theft scheme: a trucker got 30 months in federal prison for his role.
Prosecutors say that ring used real freight assignments and trucking companies to steal loads in Southern California.
14 people charged in a separate $22.5 million ring that allegedly stopped moving freight trains.
Stolen sneakers, tools and electronics were traced through SoCal storage sites into resale markets; vet partners closely.

sections.heading: Port strike threat eases
bullets: Tentative union deal reached at LA-Long Beach, the busiest U.S. container port complex.
The accord follows more than a year of bargaining, including federally mediated talks.
Drayage and SoCal carriers face less near-term risk of a sudden freight stoppage.

sections.heading: Pre-Thanksgiving capacity watch
bullets: Tender rejections typically rise slightly before Thanksgiving, per FreightWaves SONAR data.
FreightWaves projects rejections could top 14% as low inventories spur last-minute shipping.
Tighter capacity could give small carriers more leverage on holiday spot loads.

sections.heading: Broker liability case advances
bullets: Split ruling: J.B. Hunt's brokerage won one issue and lost one in Arizona federal court.
The case is shaping up as a key test after Montgomery vs. Caribe Transport II.
Outcomes could shift how brokers screen carriers, affecting load access for small fleets.

brief.seo_description: Diesel falls to $5.937, two cargo theft cases in court, LA-Long Beach strike averted, and holiday capacity tightens for small trucking fleets.
